title: Helping Youths Overcome Social Media and Gaming Addictions
what_it_is: Helping Youths Overcome Social Media and Gaming Addictions

sections.label: Youth social media gaming addiction
sections.summary: MOH is reviewing medical evidence on youth social media and gaming addictions and access to community addiction support services, with counselling programmes available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry tracks social media and gaming addictions amongst youths; and (b) whether the Ministry is considering any measures to help youth overcome such addiction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: There are youth counselling and intervention programmes available for those seeking help, such as TOUCH Community Services and WE CARE Community Services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: MOH is working with experts to review the latest medical evidence for social media and gaming addictions amongst youths and working with the National Council of Social Service to review access to addiction support services in the community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Otherwise, it will be very difficult to actually force someone to receive any form of intervention or care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But if parents are struggling with where to start to begin the journey of helping their child, they could go to our Mindline.sg website and take a look at some of the resources that are available there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Sometimes, it may have to begin with some befriending, so that the child or the adolescent gets comfortable with someone they feel they can open up to and trust, and then gradually bring them on board to receive treatment.
